statement: Libogc places both register writes and 0x18 audio blocks into a single command queue, with the next command dispatched when a matching input 0x22 ACK completes the current one. Its speaker-data builder sets the 20-byte length field but not the bit 1 ACK-request flag; by contrast the simple enable and mute command builder sets bit 1. Therefore a virtual target that never acknowledges queued 0x18 data risks stalling subsequent audio/control in this particular consumer. This is a source-level deadlock risk, not proof that real hardware sends a successful ACK for every speaker-data block.

applicability.revision: Original Wii Remote consumer protocol paths; no retail revision measured
